newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures close sharply lower.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures closed sharply lower due to a sharp, relentless selloff in bellwether technology stocks, traders and analysts said.
IBM Corp, Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp were the key technology stocks that traders said were dragging the March Standard & Poor's 500 contract toward the 800.00 level.
"Those stocks led the market up, and they are leading the market down," one S&P futures floor trader said.
"I see no reason to own these things at these levels," he said when asked whether he thought those stocks would continue to decline after already steep losses.
Jay Hohmann, head of stock index futures trading at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, has been noting the bearish chart formations of those individual tech stocks for the last week.
"Those issues crested well before S&Ps made their highs," he said. "I don't think you can dismiss the sheer psychological aspect that that sends to the market."
March S&Ps fell to 801.80, as some traders had anticipated earlier in the session when the contract broke below the 808.40 area.
"There is just nothing from 808.00 to 801.00," another floor trader said.

Sell-stop orders were particularly heavy at 807.00, and traders noted a steady stream of dealer selling throughout the day. One major U.S. firm alone had sold about 1,500 contracts by early afternoon.
Traders also noted arbitrage sell programs after midday, which occurred at a 1.00- to 1.40-point premium to the cash index.
But in typical fashion, the market's heaviest selling pressure was generated in the final hour of pit trade after U.S. bond futures closed for the day at 1400 CST/2000 GMT.
March T-bonds, which S&P futures traders were closely tracking, continued to erode into their close and settled near the day's low.

Despite signs of low inflationary pressures, some traders still think the U.S. Federal Reserve could raise rates later in the year. Higher U.S. interest rates could increase the attractiveness of U.S. government securities and lead investors to shift money out of the stock market.
Toward the end of Thursday's session, one floor trader said March S&Ps could possibly break below 800.00. Such a break, he said, would be followed by a rapid descent to the 780.00 area.
Hohmann was anticipating that cash S&Ps would fall about five percent to 760.00 in the near to intermediate term.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were off 10.05 points at 804.25, KCBT Value Lines were 4.10 lower at 715.00, NYSE Composites were 5.00 lower at 421.35, Nikkeis were up 420 to 19,020, Midcap 400s were off 2.90 at 266.80 and Nasdaq 100s fell 16.55 at 883.45.
